card: This PR updates the getorphantxs RPC help text to use verbosity instead of the removed verbose parameter name in its output headings, fixing an unknown named parameter error when users follow the help example. It also switches getorphantxs to standard RPC schema argument type validation and removes the unused allow_bool flag from ParseVerbosity across remaining callers. The change resolves inaccurate RPC documentation and aligns type checking with standard RPC conventions.
changed_since_previous: None; the previous description was generated without the patch diff and accurately described these commits.
evidence: Commit cfd652ae52: "The headings still refer to the removed verbose alias, so following the help and passing verbose=1 returns Unknown named parameter verbose."
Commit e913ca2b16: "estimatesmartfee is the only caller that asks ParseVerbosity to reject booleans, and its options type check already rejects them before the call."
problem: PR #31043 removed the `verbose` parameter alias from `getorphantxs`, but the help output headings still referenced `for verbose = N`. Users copying the parameter name from help encounter `Unknown named parameter verbose`. Additionally, `getorphantxs` bypassed schema type checking using `skip_type_check = true` to return a custom error message on boolean inputs.

risk.why: Alters RPC help text and changes error messages for invalid input types on getorphantxs without affecting valid RPC behavior.

summary: Updates `getorphantxs` RPC help text headings to reference `verbosity` instead of the removed `verbose` parameter. Switches `getorphantxs` to use standard RPC schema type checking and defaults rather than manual parsing, and removes the unused `allow_bool` parameter from `ParseVerbosity`.
